title: Streaming standby on PostgreSQL 16.14 stops applying WAL at MultiXactOffsetSLRU when primary is 16.8
body: I accidentally ran a PostgreSQL 16.14 physical streaming standby against a non-upgraded 16.8 primary on Ubuntu 22.04. WAL continues arriving and receive/write/flush remain current, but replay stops and the lag grows to about 9 GB. The startup process repeatedly reports wait_event_type LWLock and wait_event MultiXactOffsetSLRU and is parked in futex_wait_queue. After resetting SLRU statistics and waiting under live streaming, pg_stat_slru reports no MultiXactOffset or MultiXactMember reads, writes, hits, or zeroing. There are no standby readers, MultiXact age on the primary is small, and other 16.8 replicas are unaffected. Restarting only clears the block until the standby catches up and encounters it again. Downgrading this standby to 16.12 with the same data directory restored replay initially.

symptoms_visible: On the 16.14 standby, receive LSN keeps advancing while replay LSN remains frozen and replay lag grows to about 9 GB.
The startup process repeatedly waits on LWLock:MultiXactOffsetSLRU and is parked in futex_wait_queue, while pg_stat_slru records no MultiXact activity.
Restarting lets replay resume only until the standby catches up and blocks again; using the 16.12 binary initially restored replay.
N0.label: N0 cross-version WAL replay stall reported

symptoms_visible: After more than 12 hours on 16.12, recovery stops with 'could not access status of transaction' and a short read from pg_multixact/offsets/017C while replaying a MultiXact CREATE_ID record.
N1_x.label: N1_x downgrade aftermath

symptoms_visible: The affected startup process remains parked while replaying WAL, with receive continuing ahead of replay.
N2.label: N2 startup backtrace collected

symptoms_visible: The 16.14 startup process is waiting in SimpleLruWriteAll while replaying a MultiXact CREATE_ID WAL record.
The temporary 16.12 downgrade later stops recovery with a short read from a MultiXact offsets file.
N3.label: N3 matching WAL record identified

symptoms_visible: In the cross-version reproductions, the unpatched standby stops at the MultiXact offsets page boundary, while the provided patched build replays all WAL and catches up.
N4.label: N4 candidate patch verified in reproductions

symptoms_visible: I have not yet retested my affected standby with a build containing the landed locking fix.
N_terminal.label: terminal fix applied upstream without reporter retest

solution.intent: Keep the standby pinned to PostgreSQL 16.12 as the durable resolution for the 16.14 replay stall.
solution.concrete_example: Continue running the standby with the 16.12 binary because replay resumed after the downgrade.

edges.comment: Opening report and c4, both from Radim's deployment: the 16.12 downgrade initially restored replay but later failed recovery with a short read from pg_multixact/offsets. It is not a durable fix.

question_patterns: Can you capture a debugger backtrace of the hanging startup process with debug symbols?
What are the PostgreSQL frames beneath LWLockAcquire in the blocked startup process?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I captured the blocked startup process. The PostgreSQL frames are LWLockAcquire in exclusive mode, called by SimpleLruWriteAll(MultiXactOffsetCtl, false), then RecordNewMultiXact, multixact_redo, ApplyWalRecord, PerformWalRecovery, and StartupXLOG.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: My backtrace never enters SimpleLruWriteAll or RecordNewMultiXact; it is blocked in filesystem I/O while reading a WAL segment.
The same PostgreSQL frames appear, but some libc frames and addresses differ because the trace came from another Ubuntu build.

edges.comment: c1 and c5: backtraces came from affected operators, including a fuller trace supplied by the opening reporter's side. Multi-user evidence is folded into one simulated user side without treating the separate hosts as one deployment.

question_patterns: Can you collect a symbolic backtrace from an affected startup process?
Which PostgreSQL functions appear below the LWLock wait?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The trace enters LWLockAcquire from SimpleLruWriteAll(MultiXactOffsetCtl, false), called by RecordNewMultiXact, multixact_redo, and WAL recovery.

question_patterns: Can you dump the WAL around the last replayed LSN and paste the record where recovery stops?
What does pg_waldump show at the blocked replay location?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The matching pg_waldump entry is a MultiXact CREATE_ID record for multi 79871 at offset 218449 with two members. The startup backtrace shows RecordNewMultiXact handling the same values.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The record at the blocked location is a heap update and there is no MultiXact CREATE_ID record nearby.
I reproduced the same stack on a different page boundary with different MultiXact and offset numbers.

edges.comment: c4-c6: Radim reported the later 16.12 recovery error and supplied additional data; the symbolic trace and WAL dump tie the original 16.14 wait to a specific CREATE_ID replay record.

question_patterns: Can you run pg_waldump around the last replayed LSN and paste the record associated with the blocked stack?
Which WAL record was RecordNewMultiXact replaying when the startup process stopped?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The dump has a matching MultiXact CREATE_ID record: multi 79871, offset 218449, two members. Those values also appear in the RecordNewMultiXact frame.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The WAL dump contains no MultiXact records around the last replayed LSN.
The same CREATE_ID pattern occurs at another offsets page boundary with different numeric IDs.

edges.comment: c5-c6: raw WAL and debugger values supplied by affected operators. Recognizing that the record is at the final MultiXact offset on its page is engineer-side analysis, not part of the user's answer.

question_patterns: Can you run the supplied patch through a cross-version replay test that crosses a MultiXact offsets page boundary and report both patched and unpatched results?
Please compare the same reproduction workload on an unpatched build and the provided patched build.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I generated 2500 MultiXacts on an older primary, took a base backup, generated another 2500, and started the newer standby. Without the change, startup deadlocks. With the change, the standby catches up, and the DEBUG1 output says the next offsets page was not initialized and is being initialized.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Both the unpatched and patched builds deadlock at the same MultiXact page boundary.
The patched build catches up using 2300 MultiXacts instead of 2500, while still crossing the page boundary.

question_patterns: Can someone independently test the supplied patch with an older primary and a newer assertion-enabled standby?
Please reproduce this on a fresh environment and report whether the patched standby completes replay.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: In a fresh setup with a 16.8 primary and an assertion-enabled 16.14 standby, about 2300 MultiXacts crossed the offsets page boundary. Without the patch, startup deadlocked at RecordNewMultiXact for multi 2047. With the patch, the standby replayed all WAL and caught up.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The independently patched standby still deadlocks at RecordNewMultiXact.

edges.comment: c13 and c15: pre-landing verification came from maintainers and a separate test operator, not from Radim's production standby. Their raw patched/unpatched outcomes are folded into the user side as relayed test evidence, without claiming that the original reporter verified the fix.

solution.intent: Fix the back-branch recovery compatibility path by delaying acquisition of the MultiXact offsets SLRU lock until after the flush and missing-page check, matching the newer-branch locking order and preserving the protective flush.
solution.concrete_example: Adjust RecordNewMultiXact so the compatibility path can run SimpleLruWriteAll before taking MultiXactOffsetSLRULock, then acquire the lock at the later point used by newer branches. Apply the change to the affected supported back branches and ask the reporter to retest using a build that contains it.
solution.inference_hint: Engineers mapped the matching backtrace and WAL record to the page-boundary compatibility path. RecordNewMultiXact already holds MultiXactOffsetSLRULock when SimpleLruWriteAll attempts to acquire that same SLRU control lock, causing a self-deadlock before any SLRU I/O. They initially considered removing the flush, then withdrew that approach because a dirty offsets page created by out-of-order CREATE_ID replay may not yet exist on disk. The accepted fix instead moves the original lock acquisition later, preserving the flush and physical-page check.

edges.comment: c3 and c6-c16 establish the final diagnosis and accepted locking change. The earlier remove-SimpleLruWriteAll proposal was explicitly walked back in c8; the final patch moves lock acquisition later and was applied to the affected supported branches in c16. The original reporter did not subsequently confirm a fixed build on their own standby, so this terminal state records upstream application and third-party tests without declaring the reporter's system resolved.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted root cause: during cross-version MultiXact CREATE_ID replay at an offsets page boundary, RecordNewMultiXact holds MultiXactOffsetSLRULock and calls SimpleLruWriteAll, which attempts to acquire the same SLRU control lock and self-deadlocks before any SLRU I/O.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: frozen replay with advancing receive, the MultiXactOffsetSLRU wait with zero SLRU activity, the SimpleLruWriteAll-to-RecordNewMultiXact backtrace, and the matching CREATE_ID WAL record.

The fix must move the original lock acquisition later so the flush and physical-page existence check occur without recursively acquiring the same lock, while preserving the flush needed to account for dirty SLRU pages.
Must not present restarting the standby or remaining downgraded on the older binary as a durable resolution; restart recurred and the downgraded standby later failed recovery.

Must not recommend simply removing SimpleLruWriteAll: that preliminary approach was withdrawn because out-of-order replay can leave a relevant dirty offsets page that is not yet visible to the physical-file check.

Must ask the original reporter to verify on a build containing the fix before declaring their deployment resolved; separate reproduction tests and upstream application do not constitute reporter confirmation.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced PostgreSQL operator who can inspect replication LSNs and wait events, reset and read SLRU statistics, capture kernel and debugger stacks, run pg_waldump, swap minor-version binaries against an existing data directory, and discuss PITR safety.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, evidence-driven, and cooperative. Provides exact commands, counters, stack frames, WAL locations, and configuration details; distinguishes temporary symptom relief from sustained recovery and follows up when a workaround exposes another failure.
